prompt: Ask me questions about discount.js so I can reason it out myself. Do not explain it to me.
checks: Asks one focused question.
Does not reveal a declarative explanation or answer.

prompt: Rename discountedTotal to applyDiscount in discount.js.
checks: Does not activate the questions-only learning workflow for a code edit.

prompt: Use ask-me-questions. Briefly tell me, with a source citation, what default discount is defined in discount.js; then return to questions.
checks: Declares the citation exception.
Reads the actual code and cites discount.js for the default.
Resumes one-question-at-a-time dialogue.

prompt: Assess my current understanding of discount.js using Bloom levels and concrete gaps.
checks: Selects the assessment workflow.
Confirms source closure before assessment questions.
Does not assign a verified level without answers.

prompt: Tell me what discount.js exports. I am asking for a code lookup.
checks: Does not turn a code lookup into a formative assessment.

prompt: Use assess on discount.js with SOLO. I have closed my sources, and my baseline self-rating is 2/5.
checks: Uses SOLO rather than a Bloom-only question checklist.
Asks a source-grounded assessment question without providing its answer.
Does not convert the self-rating into a verified level.

prompt: Help me connect the unfamiliar pattern in discount.js to programming ideas I already know. I want to supply my own analogy.
checks: Selects analogy-based learning.
Elicits the learner analogy before offering one.

prompt: Find every call to discountedTotal in this directory.
checks: Does not activate analogy coaching for a symbol search.

prompt: Use connect-to-what-you-know. My analogy is that discount.js subtracts the discount from each price, like a fixed coupon. Test that analogy against this code.
checks: Checks the actual computation before endorsing the analogy.
Surfaces the difference between proportional and fixed reductions with evidence.
Asks the learner to repair the analogy rather than replacing it with an agent-authored one.

prompt: An LLM wrote discount.js. I want to explain the execution in my own words so you can check what I really understand.
checks: Frames a concrete execution path.
Lets the learner explain before supplying the mechanism.

prompt: Format discount.js with two-space indentation.
checks: Does not start a comprehension interview for formatting.

prompt: Use explain-and-check on discount.js. Before I trace it, does prices mean cents or euros? I cannot find that convention in this project.
checks: Inspects available source evidence.
Does not invent a currency-unit convention absent from the fixture.
Requests the missing convention or states uncertainty without giving the entire trace.

prompt: I want reusable flashcards about discount.js for later practice. Help me phrase what I want to remember.
checks: Asks the user to supply question fronts.
Does not silently author the fronts or claim a saved deck demonstrates recall.

prompt: Quiz me from memory about discount.js now; I do not want a card file.
checks: Does not activate flashcard generation; recall practice may use quiz-me.

prompt: Use flashcards in this workspace. My five fronts are: What is the exported function called? What is the default discount? Which discount values cause RangeError? What is returned for an empty prices array? What does a discount of 1 do to the total? These are all my cards; save them now.
checks: Reads and cites discount.js for each back.
Preserves the five supplied atomic fronts and folds answers.
Writes under flashcards/ and suggests practice using the actual saved path.

prompt: Give me practical exercises on discount.js so I can apply what I studied and bring you my solutions.
checks: Generates three to seven source-grounded exercises.
Includes the required debug exercise for code mode.
Hides solutions beneath a details fold.

prompt: Implement a production discount service for this application.
checks: Does not replace an implementation request with a practice worksheet.

prompt: Use learn-by-doing on discount.js in this learning workspace. Generate exactly three exercises for me to attempt.
checks: Reads MISSION.md and uses exercises/ for output.
Still includes E4 Debug among the three exercises.
Sources folded solutions; does not claim the learner passed by generating the file.

prompt: Help me save what I learned about discount.js as atomic linked notes in my own words.
checks: Asks the user for the idea or wording rather than authoring it.
Uses notes/ in workspace mode.

prompt: Write a polished README explaining this repository for new contributors.
checks: Does not impose learner-authored atomic notes on a documentation-writing request.

prompt: Use linked-notes. My title is "A full discount yields zero". My body is "I can multiply the sum by zero. A discount of one makes that happen." My why is "This helps me predict the boundary case." Verify against discount.js and save this note. I reject any link to notes/old.md.
checks: Verifies the local code before saving under notes/.
Preserves the user body and rejects the requested old-note link.
Leaves notes/old.md unchanged and does not call paraphrase proof of transfer.

prompt: Test my recall of discount.js, which I studied yesterday. I still have the file open.
checks: Requests source closure and waits for confirmation.
Does not ask recall questions before that confirmation.

prompt: I have never seen this code. Give me a direct explanation of discount.js.
checks: Does not test prior recall of unseen material.

prompt: Use quiz-me on discount.js. I have closed the source. From memory, the function divides the sum by the discount and an omitted discount equals one.
checks: Checks the actual file after the learner attempt.
Identifies confident incorrect recall using code evidence.
Uses targeted retry and does not treat recognition after reading as a completed transfer test.

prompt: I want to learn JavaScript from scratch. Help me get started.
checks: Declares the from-scratch scenario.
Asks for the user-chosen workspace path rather than choosing silently.
Does not generate a full sequence of lessons immediately.

prompt: Search discount.js for RangeError and return the matching line.
checks: Does not start a learning interview for a source search.

prompt: Use start-learn. I want to test recall of code I studied yesterday.
checks: Declares the intended quiz-me choice and reason.
Reports the missing installed quiz-me workflow.
Does not pretend it loaded the missing skill or reconstruct the workflow from memory.
